description.narrative: Liberia Decentralization Support Program II (LDSP II), implemented by UNDP as the agreement partner for Sida, builds on previous support towards Liberia's decentralization process (LDSP I, 2016-2020). LDSP II has been running since 2020 and Sweden will enter as a donor during the period 2022-2024. Overall, the programme aims to reach the following outcomes: Outcome 1: LGA reforms implemented through enhanced participation of stakeholders (male, female, PWDs) in decision-making and service delivery, Outcome 2: Local government institutions and services are fully devolved at the assigned levels of government, Outcome 3: County Service Centers empowered and capacitated for improved service delivery at the sub-national level. Outcome 4: Legal and Regulatory Reforms developed and implemented to sustain decentralization. Outcome 5: Programme management support, coordination, and monitoring strengthened. Swedish support primarily focuses on fiscal decentralization.

Liberia Decentralization Support Programme II (LDSP II), som genomförs av UNDP som avtalspart för Sida, bygger på ett tidigare stöd till Liberias decentraliseringsprocess (LDSP I, 2016-2020). LDSP II har pågått sedan 2020 och Sverige kommer in som givare under perioden 2022-2024. Övergripande väntas insatsen bidra till följande resultat: 1. Reformer inom lagen för lokalförvaltning (Local Government Act) implementeras med ett ökat deltagande av rättighetsbärare (kvinnor, män och personer med funktionsvariationer) i beslutsfattande och i tillhandahållandet av tjänster 2. Lokala, statliga institutioner och tjänster är fullt ut delegerade till tilldelade myndighetsnivåer 3. Lokala servicekontor (County Service Centers) stärks och ges ökad kapacitet för förbättrad leverans av tjänster på lokal nivå 4. Rättsliga och regulatoriska reformer utvecklas och implementeras för att upprätthålla decentralisering 5. Stärkt programledningsstöd, samordning och uppföljning. Sveriges stöd till insatsen fokuserar främst på finansiell decentralisering.

description.narrative:
While the contribution from the Swedish embassy is primarily focusing on the fiscal decentralisation (outcome 4), there are results in all areas of the program. Some results which were shown during 2024 (the last year of reporting) included:
-To facilitate the implementation of the Revenue Sharing Act (RSA), townhall meetings were held (engaging approx. 2,500 citizens in 39 meetings), radio talk shows and jingles were aired on radio and information material was distributed in 10 counties. Also, the two contracted CSOs (IREDD and InfoQUest) conducted 12 strategic advocacy engagement dialogues with 272 stakeholders (legislature, MFDP, MIA, LRA, GC) to enhance their understanding of the legal regulatory framework.
-Four regional policy dialogues on the RSA were organised, targeting local government officials, members of the County Councils and communitybased CSOs (152 participants). The dialogues enhanced improved understanding of the RSA on mechanisms for sustaining fiscal decentralization, its importance to domestic resource mobilization, incentives associated with the payment of taxes, and stakeholders ownership of the RSA at the local level.
-Key informant interviews conducted with County Council members in Margibi, Bong, Bomi, and Grand Cape Mount counties revealed that the financial management and revenue sharing trainings have contributed to improved understanding of the government fiscal management procedures, and an understanding of the various processes in managing government resources, which will aid in raising revenue and contribute to improved governance and development.
-The second phase of the Real Property Tax Revenue Sharing Project began. Tax agents have captured more than 7,700 properties. Tax agents also incorporated awareness activities, carried out outreach activities in the communities and educated property owners before soliciting their property information.
-The project collaborated with the Fiscal Decentralization Unit at the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning and conducted a financial management training for newly appointed local government officials (81 participants). Also, a similar training was organised for four County Treasuries.
-The RSA Regulations were also validated, endorsed by the cabinet, approved by the Minister of Finance and Development Planning thus operationalizing Revenue Sharing modalities between central and local government units.
-An orientation on Local Government for all local government structures was conducted. In total, 251 civil servants at local level enhanced their capacities. The aim was to promote effective and efficient administrative, fiscal, and political functions at the local and sublocal levels. As an extension of the Local Government Orientation, the National Council of Chiefs was setup.
-In February of 2024, the Ministry of Transport Vehicle and Drivers License Hub was setup in Ganta, Nimba County and training provided for 30 staff.
-One solar power system was installed at the Grand Kru County Service Center (CSC) and one solar power system at Lofa CSC was repaired after being damaged due to equipment overload. This contributed to enhanced public service delivery, improved security and increased revenue generation. Training was also provided to technicians to enhance maintenance of solar systems.
-The Ministry of Internal Affairs in collaboration with the Governance Commission, Law Reform Commission, Office of the Legal Advisor to the President organized a 4day dialogue with the Senate and House of Representative Committees on Good Governance on the enactment of the Ministry of Local Government Bill. The dialogue resulted in the amendment of 12 provisions in the bill. A comprehensive bill has been produced, enacted by the Senate and sent to the House of Representative for concurrence.
-The rollout of the Performance Management and Compliance System (PMCS) was supported by the project, for instance by providing training to 280 focal persons. The aim of the PMCS is to establish a robust framework for holding Cabinet Ministers and Heads of MACs accountable for their actions and decisions, fostering a culture of responsibility, accountability, and responsiveness to the needs of the Liberian citizens they serve.
-The Inter-Ministerial Committee on Decentralization (IMCD) meeting was once again organised. The meeting concluded with President Boakais commitment to the implementation of decentralization reforms including the operationalization of the Revenue Sharing Act and its regulations, and the enforcement of the Local Government Act.
